variant.stem_override: A 62-year-old Black or African American man with non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy is seen in clinic for a new diagnosis of heart failure. Echocardiogram shows a left ventricular ejection fraction of 28%, mildly dilated left ventricle, and no significant valvular disease. He is NYHA class II–III on exertion. Vital signs: BP 118/72 mmHg, HR 78 bpm, weight 82 kg. Labs: serum potassium 4.1 mmol/L, eGFR 68 mL/min/1.73 m^2, NT-proBNP 1,400 pg/mL. He has no diabetes and is not on any cardiac medications.
variant.rationale_for_variant: Only the patient's race was changed to Black or African American; all clinical data, vital signs, lab values, and the clinical question remain identical. The correct answer (B) is unchanged because the 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA four-pillar GDMT recommendations apply uniformly regardless of race, and the ARNI-preferred strategy supersedes the historically race-specific ACEi/hydralazine-nitrate consideration (which applies only when ARNI/ACEi/ARB are not tolerated). This variant probes whether test-takers incorrectly anchor on race to select a different regimen (e.g., hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate) rather than applying universal guideline-directed therapy.
